name: Maldives
tagline: Overwater mornings, glowing shorelines — and a free visa on arrival
hero_description: The Maldives is what the phrase 'island paradise' was coined for: a thousand-plus coral islands scattered in turquoise rings, where your villa stands on stilts over the lagoon and the house reef starts metres from your ladder. For Indian travellers it's surprisingly easy — a free 30-day visa on arrival and a short flight from the metros — and in the wet season, some shorelines literally glow at night.
best_time_to_visit: November to April for the dry high season of calm seas and maximum sun; June to October brings lower rates and the best odds of bioluminescent 'Sea of Stars' shorelines on dark new-moon nights.

top_attractions.name: Overwater villas
top_attractions.description: The signature Maldivian stay — stilted villas over the lagoon, many with glass floor panels and a private ladder straight into the water below.

top_attractions.name: House-reef snorkelling
top_attractions.description: On many islands the reef ledge sits metres from the sand — swim out to parrotfish, rays and turtles before breakfast, no boat required.

top_attractions.name: The 'Sea of Stars'
top_attractions.description: Bioluminescent plankton that flare blue when the water is disturbed — famously seen at Vaadhoo Island, most likely from June to October on new-moon nights (a matter of luck, never a guarantee).

top_attractions.name: Sandbank picnics
top_attractions.description: A dhoni drops you on a bare white sandbank in open turquoise — just the two of you, a picnic, and horizon in every direction.

top_attractions.name: Manta and whale-shark waters
top_attractions.description: Certain atolls host seasonal gatherings — Baa Atoll's Hanifaru Bay, inside a UNESCO biosphere reserve, is famous for mass manta feeding events.

top_attractions.name: Malé old town
top_attractions.description: One of the world's most densely packed small islands — its fish market bustle and the Old Friday Mosque, built from carved coral stone in 1658, make a worthwhile half-day between flights.

activities: Waking up in an overwater villa with lagoon ladder access
Snorkelling the house reef straight off the beach
Sunset dolphin cruise aboard a traditional dhoni
Seaplane transfer with aerial atoll views
Diving day trips timed to manta and whale-shark seasons
Half-day in Malé — fish market and the coral-stone Old Friday Mosque
